categories.main_business_segments: Create Restaurants Holdings operates primarily in the restaurant business, managing a diverse portfolio of brands across casual dining, food courts, izakaya (Japanese pubs), bakeries, and contract food services such as golf course and leisure facility restaurants. The group is structured into four main categories: CR (multi-brand restaurants and food courts), SFP (izakaya and pubs), Specialty Brands (niche and regional concepts), and Overseas (international operations in North America and Asia).
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company emphasizes operational excellence in multi-brand restaurant management, leveraging digital transformation (DX) tools such as mobile ordering, AI-based reservation systems, and serving robots to enhance productivity and customer experience. It also focuses on in-house store design and construction management, strict food safety protocols, and centralized procurement and logistics for efficiency and quality control.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Key customers include general consumers and families visiting shopping centers, train stations, airports, and urban entertainment districts, as well as users of golf courses and leisure facilities. The company targets both domestic Japanese diners and international customers, including inbound tourists and local patrons in overseas markets such as the US, Singapore, Hong Kong, and Taiwan.
categories.geographic_coverage: The group’s core operations are in Japan, with a growing presence in North America (notably California and Arizona) and Asia (Singapore, Hong Kong, Taiwan). As of the end of FY2025, the company operated 1,116 stores, including 70 overseas locations, and plans further expansion in Europe and other regions.
categories.supply_chain_position: Create Restaurants Holdings is positioned downstream in the supply chain, directly operating and managing end-customer-facing restaurants and food service outlets. It also engages in contract food services and has centralized procurement and logistics functions to support its outlets.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include evolving the multi-brand, multi-location model, accelerating group synergy through M&A, expanding overseas, and strengthening the 'federal management' approach. The company is investing in DX (digital transformation), human capital, and sustainability, with a focus on food safety, supply chain resilience, and environmental initiatives such as CO2 reduction and food waste minimization. There is no mention of traditional R&D; innovation is driven by business model evolution, new brand development, and technology adoption.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is primarily generated from direct restaurant sales (food and beverage), contract food service operations, and, to a lesser extent, franchise and management fees. The company also receives income from brand licensing, store management, and food product sales (including souvenirs and packaged goods).
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Create Restaurants Holdings is a leading multi-brand restaurant operator in Japan, competing with other large food service groups such as Skylark, Colowide, and Zensho. Its strength lies in its diversified brand portfolio, flexible location strategy, and ability to quickly adapt to market changes through M&A and operational innovation.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For FY2025, consolidated revenue reached ¥156.4 billion (up 7.3% YoY), with operating profit of ¥8.5 billion (up 20.2% YoY) and net profit attributable to owners of ¥5.6 billion (up 10.9% YoY). The company has shown strong post-pandemic recovery and steady growth, with a five-year CAGR in revenue and profit, and targets further expansion to ¥165 billion in sales and ¥9.6 billion in operating profit by FY2026.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: The company differentiates itself through a highly diversified, multi-brand portfolio that allows rapid adaptation to changing consumer trends and locations. Its strengths include operational flexibility, strong M&A execution, robust food safety and sustainability practices, and the ability to deliver a wide range of dining experiences from casual to specialty concepts, both domestically and internationally.
